texts.preamble: Shri Sachin B.G vs Tata Aig General Insurance Company on 15 April, 2019 In The Court Of Iii Addl.Judge And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Court Of Small Causes Bengaluru (Scch-18) Dated: This the 15th day of April 2019 Present: Sri.Mahantesh S.Dargad B.Sc., LL.B.,(Spl) Iii Addl. Judge & Member, Mact Court Of Small Causes, Bengaluru. M.V.C.No.2945/2018 Petitioner Shri Sachin B.G., Son of Gangaraju B.C., Aged about 24 years, No.78, Bandihalli, Huliyurdurga, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur-572 123. (By Pleader Shri Puttaswamy H.) V/s. Respondents 1.Tata Aig General Insurance Company Limited, Race Course Road, Left to No.59, 3rd floor, Jp & Dj Arcade, Millers Road, Bengaluru-560 054. 2 Scch-18 Mvc 2945/2018 Policy No.0146356478 Valid from 30.8.2017 to 29.8.2018. (By Pleader Shri Janardhana Reddy) 2.Lingaraju H.N., Son of Late Ningappa, Hebbaralu (Village & Post) Maddur Taluk, Mandya District. (Owner of the vehicle bearing No.KA-11- Ef-3815) (Exparte) Shri Sachin B.G vs Tata Aig General Insurance Company on 15 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7056894/ 1 J U D G M E N T
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation amount of Rs.12,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the petition are as under: On 22.2.2018 at about 8.45 p.m. the petitioner was a pillion rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-11-EF-3815. The rider was proceeding on Hosahalli road, Dodda Gollarahatti, Bengaluru at that time, the rider of the said vehicle rode the same in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and safety of others and jumped the path holes and apply the sudden break. As a result of the forced impact, the petitioner was thrown out fell down and sustained grievous injuries on the vital parts of the body. Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Srikrishna Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein after first aid treatment was offered and admitted as an inpatient. 3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 24 years, electrician and earning a sum of Rs.18,000/- per month. The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor bike bearing No.KA-11-EF-3815. Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation. Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost. 4. In response to the petition notice, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court and the respondent No.1 has appeared before the court and filed its written statement. 5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 are as under: The respondent No.1 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts. Further this respondent has denied about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No. ka-11-ef- 3815 and its validity. Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition. Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the claim petition as against this respondent with cost. 6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed: 7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P10, and doctor is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P11 to Ex.P13. 8. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent No.1 has not examined any witness on its behalf.
texts.arguments: Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of S. 134 and S. 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars. Further contended that the rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the same. During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner argued by reiterating the contents of petition and also evidence put forth by PW1 & PW2. Further he argued that, to prove the disablement, the petitioner has examined Dr.Aruju S.Pakash as PW2, who has assessed 46.8% of left upper limb and 15.6% of whole body disability. Further he argued that the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence. Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition. 12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has denied the accident in toto, hence, prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondent No.1. 17. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others). 24. The contention of the petitioner is that, he has spent huge amount of Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses. 25. Further contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 24 years, working as a Electrician and getting an income of Rs.18,000/- per month.
